title: Mirabel and the Thorn
premise: Astrid Dravenmoor has spent his life mapping the Thornfell mountains and the smuggler roads that thread them, keeping everyone at arm's length since the fever took his family. When a mute child named Mirabel appears at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom, he learns she is a soul sold to the Undercourt beneath the mountain, and that her borrowed time runs out at the winter solstice. Guided by a disgraced Undercourt exile and his own forbidden knowledge of the deep roads, Astrid descends to bargain, cheat, and steal her back. He succeeds, but only by offering the court a soul of equal weight — his own memories of everyone he ever loved — and in the end, with Mirabel's hand in his and no past left to grieve, he chooses to build a new belonging from nothing.
about_author: Felix Ravensworth is the pen name of a former alpine trail surveyor who spent a decade sketching passes no government would officially acknowledge. Their fiction blends cartographic precision with folklore collected in mountain taverns across three continents.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A blizzard drives Astrid home early from surveying; on his doorstep sits a girl of seven or eight, frostbitten but unafraid, who speaks in a tongue that makes his maps' oldest marginalia glow. The emotional beat: wary curiosity cracking open a long-sealed loneliness.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Astrid and Mirabel. Astrid consults Vessa, a half-blind archivist, who identifies the language as Undercourt speech and goes pale: the child is a sold soul, marked for collection at solstice. Beat: dread replacing wonder as Astrid realizes helping her means defying something beneath the world.

chapters.title: The Collector Comes Early
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, rendered in her strange, literal perception. A gray-faced Collector arrives ahead of schedule; Astrid hides Mirabel in the smugglers' tunnels he alone knows, and the Collector leaves a black thorn in his doorframe as a promise. Beat: terror, and the first flicker of protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Exile of the Deep Roads
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid seeks out Corvane, an exiled Undercourt steward living as a ferryman, and trades a rare map for passage knowledge. Corvane warns the price of stealing back a soul must be paid in kind. Beat: reluctant alliance, the theme of price made explicit.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On the ascent, Mirabel begins remembering fragments of her life before the sale — a mother, a debt, a desperate bargain — and shares them with Astrid through drawings on his map margins. Beat: grief and tenderness; found family taking root.

chapters.title: The Tollgate of Names
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the mountain's threshold, a gate demands each traveler's true name; Astrid sacrifices his family name to pass, feeling it torn out like a tooth. Corvane notes, grimly, that the court is already collecting. Beat: rising cost, commitment beyond return.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They descend into the Undercourt, a cathedral of roots and candlelight where sold souls serve as living ledger entries. Astrid finds Mirabel's contract and discovers a loophole: a soul may be redeemed by one of greater weight, freely given. Beat: awe curdling into horror at what redemption requires.

chapters.title: Bargain and Betrayal
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid offers his own soul-weight — every memory of love he carries — but Corvane, revealed as the court's agent testing him, nearly sells them out before choosing exile's loyalty over old masters. Beat: climax of trust; betrayal averted by choice, not innocence.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Soul
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the solstice hour, the exchange begins: Astrid's memories pour out like light draining from a lamp, and Mirabel, restored, screams at him to stop — then chooses to stay beside the man who no longer knows why she matters to him. Beat: sacrifice and its terrible intimacy.

chapters.title: A Map With No Margins
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, closing with Mirabel's. Above ground again, Astrid remembers nothing of his past but finds Mirabel's drawings still inked on his maps — a story of himself written in someone else's hand. He begins a new map titled simply 'Us.' Beat: bittersweet resolution; belonging rebuilt from loss.
